hypotheses_validated.claim: Belady (now: relaxed problem without protection, bypass allowed, free initial contents, hits counted from the first measured step) is the exact optimum of that relaxed group problem and upper-bounds every online policy without prefetch over the measured window.
hypotheses_validated.evidence: tests/py/test_sim.py::test_belady_is_exactly_optimal_on_small_schedules (80 random schedules vs exhaustive search; k up to 4, 1-2 layers, speculative windows, warm-up prefix, incl. the verifier's [[2,1],[1,0],[2,1],[1,0]] cap-1 case), ::test_belady_matches_reference_on_long_traces (heap-free re-implementation, heap rebuild exercised), ::test_belady_bounds_online_policies_fuzz (120 schedules x 5 policies x 2 settings), ::test_belady_upper_bound_through_simulate_on_a_tiny_shape (incl. a simulate()-level trace where gen-1 Belady scored 0.6919 vs LRU 0.6967; new Belady 0.8104). All pass (ran). Reconstructed gen-1 Belady fails the three new Belady tests (scratch check). Repro script: 0 violations in 3000 random checks (was 76).

hypotheses_validated.claim: Prefetch protection now follows hx_store.h and engine/src/store.c: prefetched slabs are protected until used or the forward step ends; a demand evicts one only as a last resort, a prefetch never does.
hypotheses_validated.evidence: ::test_prefetched_experts_stay_protected_until_used_or_step_end and ::test_demand_evicts_unused_prefetch_only_as_last_resort pass; each fails on a variant without protection / with hard protection respectively (scratch check). With hard protection, kimi-k2/this-pc 40 GiB LFU reproduced the verifier's numbers exactly (Prefetch(0.5,4): hit 0.5918, 1.1810 tok/s; Prefetch(0.8,0): 1.3297 tok/s).

hypotheses_validated.claim: The LFU heap optimisations added for protected prefetches (held slabs and just-admitted slabs kept out of the heap until released/flushed) do not change any result.
hypotheses_validated.evidence: Scratch comparison against an eager-heap variant: identical hit/pfhit/miss/bypass/pf_issued/pf_wasted/evictions in 96 configurations (lfu, lfu-pinned; spec on/off; 4 cache/prefetch settings; 6 seeds). Without them LFU+Prefetch(0.5,4) on kimi-k2 took 39.7 s under load; with them 3.3-4.9 s.

hypotheses_validated.claim: Invalid inputs (non-positive bandwidths/int8 rate, zero drives, decay outside (0,1], pin_fraction outside [0,0.9], alpha/recall outside [0,1], negative cache/context/samples, io_threads < 1, bits outside (0,32], duplicate/negative/non-integer trace ids, oversized trace geometry) are rejected with ValueError / CLI exit 2, and huge --prefetch-extra is clamped.
hypotheses_validated.evidence: ::test_simulate_rejects_bad_inputs (24 cases), ::test_cli_rejects_bad_inputs_without_traceback (18 flag sets), ::test_trace_rejects_invalid_ids_and_huge_headers, ::test_prefetch_extra_is_clamped_and_fast (extra 10^6 / 100000 finish; previously >10 min) pass.

hypotheses_falsified.claim: (gen 1) Belady with bypass, as implemented with per-group protection and cold start, is the exact offline optimum and upper-bounds every online policy.
hypotheses_falsified.evidence: Verifier finding reproduced: cap 1, ids [[2,1],[1,0],[2,1],[1,0]] gave lru 2 hits vs belady 1; 76 of 3000 random checks had an online policy above Belady. Gen-1's exhaustive test only covered k=1, L=1.

hypotheses_falsified.claim: (gen 1 doc) Prefetched experts are protected only until the next layer has run.
hypotheses_falsified.evidence: Contradicted hx_store.h ('protected until used or the token ends') and store.c; replaced by step-long protection with last-resort demand eviction.

open_questions: Real routing skew/locality of Kimi/DeepSeek is still unknown; every sec. 8 number is SIMULATED on synthetic traces (kimi-k2/this-pc 0.6-1.7 tok/s prefetch off, 0.6-2.0 with prefetch at assumed recall 0.8).
Real recall of the engine's SHARED prefetch predictor; the simulator assumes none by default (prefetch off) and uses 0.8 where labelled.

store.c also refuses prefetches whose victim is 'hot' (LFU heat of a ~50%-of-tokens expert; LRU used this token) and assigns slots when a reader starts; not modelled (documented in sec. 6). Model it once store.c is final.
Should the engine's LFU decay default be ~0.9 instead of 0.995 (sec. 8.4)? Needs real traces.
All timing scalars are uncalibrated until T09 runs calibrate().
